title: The toggle ignores opted-in secondary assignees
problem: The new hook gates reviews through one acting reviewer. The registered resolver checks only the task creator or first resolved assignee. A secondary assignee can enable Stamphog and still receive no review. The stated behavior enables reviews when any assigned user opts in.
suggestion: Resolve all assigned organization members. Prefer the assigned task creator when that user opted in. Otherwise select the first opted-in assignee. Use this selection for both initial reviews and webhook re-reviews.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `inbox_hooks.py:20-22`'s resolver signature, its only two call sites (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:144-156` `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`, and `receivers.py:111-126` `handle_task_run_saved`), and `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (`receivers.py:159-207`). Also compared this file and `receivers.py` against the base branch (`git show master:...`, `git diff master HEAD -- products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py`).
**Found:** In the current tree, `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (`receivers.py:159-207`) picks exactly ONE user — the task creator if they are in the resolved assignee set, else the first resolved assignee (`receivers.py:206`) — before any toggle is checked. `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (`receivers.py:151-156`) then checks only that single user's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`; every other assignee's toggle is never read. `InboxActingReviewerResolver` (`inbox_hooks.py:22`) locks this in structurally: it takes one `task_created_by_id` and returns one user id, so no caller on either side of the hook can pass or receive more than one candidate. The base branch's version of `receivers.py` implements and documents the opposite, stamphog-specific rule: `_pick_stamphog_reviewer` filters ALL resolved assignees down to the opted-in ones first (`opted_in = [user for user in resolved if settings_by_user[user.id].stamphog_review_inbox_prs]`) and only then picks preferred-else-first among THEM, with the comment "Any assigned reviewer's opt-in is enough, unlike the ReviewHog review which gates on the canonical reviewer's: stamphog reads no per-user options, so narrowing it to one reviewer would drop reviews the other assignees asked for." That nuance is gone in the current code.
**Impact:** On a report with multiple assigned reviewers, if the canonical reviewer (creator-if-assigned, else first-resolved) has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` off but a different assignee has it on, `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` returns `None` and no review runs — even though the PR's own description states the intended behavior is "at least one of the assigned users has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled." This is a real, reachable gap between stated behavior and implementation, not a hypothetical edge case, and matches the finding exactly.

title: Trusted prompt reports a ready PR as draft
problem: Webhook re-reviews can run after a self-driving PR becomes ready. This block always tells the model that the PR is a draft. The prompt does not include the actual `pr.draft` value elsewhere, and it labels this claim as trusted. The model can therefore make its decision from a false PR state.
suggestion: Pass `pr.draft` to `_format_self_driving`. Add the draft sentence only when that value is true. Keep the provenance text for ready PRs. Add a test for a ready self-driving PR after a new commit.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `reviewer.py::_format_self_driving` (683-703) takes only the classification dict `cl`, built in `review_pr.py::_classify` (452-478), which carries no `draft` key; the only place `pr.draft` reaches the codebase is the telemetry field `stamphog_draft` at reviewer.py:363, never the prompt.
**Checked:** `_build_review_prompt` (449-506) calls `_format_self_driving(cl)` with no `pr` argument, so the rendered block has no way to read the PR's live draft state.
**Checked:** the webhook re-review path in `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py` — `_review_skip_reason` (218-234) and `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (144-215) — plus their call site (870-912).
**Found:** `_review_skip_reason` returns `"draft"` when `pr.get("draft")` is true, but self-driving PRs are always bot-authored (`_is_bot_authored`), so once such a PR flips to ready, the same function instead returns `"bot_author"` — still non-`None`. Since the dispatcher only calls `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` when `skip_reason is not None` (line 872), the carve-out still runs on a later `synchronize`/`reopened` event (`_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS`, line 167) after the PR is ready, and `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` performs no draft check itself — only action type, bot authorship, head repo, repo config, task linkage, and the acting reviewer's toggle.
**Found:** when that carve-out resolves, `classification["self_driving"]` is set true unconditionally (review_pr.py:477), and `_format_self_driving` then always emits "It is a draft on purpose ... draft state is not a caution signal for this PR" — with no code path that suppresses or qualifies this once the PR is actually ready.
**Found:** `test_reviewer.py::test_prompt_provenance_renders_only_for_self_driving_runs` (235-262) builds its self-driving prompt from `_pr()`, whose default is `draft=False`, and the "It is a draft on purpose" text still renders — the existing test suite already exercises this exact mismatch without asserting on it.
**Impact:** on the concrete, reachable sequence described in the PR itself (Case 2: new commits land after the PR is opened, re-review triggers) combined with the PR later turning ready, the LLM reviewer is fed a TRUSTED block asserting a false PR state and told to disregard draft status as a caution signal for a PR that is no longer draft. This is a real correctness bug in prompt construction, not a speculative edge case, since the webhook path that reaches it is exactly the one this PR adds.

title: A Stamphog outage can delay every settings response
problem: The serializer queries the Stamphog product database for every GET and PATCH. Product database connections can wait three seconds before failure. The shared breaker opens only after several failures. Concurrent requests can therefore hold web workers even though this handler later returns false. The 200 response also hides the outage as a disconnected state. The Kea loader does not retry a successful load, so the switch stays disabled after recovery.
suggestion: Move this check to a separate Stamphog status request or a cached snapshot. Return distinct loading, unavailable, and disconnected states. Add a bounded retry for unavailable status. Keep ReviewHog settings requests independent from the Stamphog database.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `posthog/db_circuit_breaker.py`, `posthog/db_backends/failopen/base.py`, and `posthog/settings/data_stores.py:172-220` for how product-database connections behave on an outage. Checked `products/db_routing.yaml` and `StamphogRepoConfig`'s `ProductTeamModel` base to confirm `has_reviewable_repo_config` reads through the routed `stamphog_db_reader` alias, not the main database. Checked `products/review_hog/frontend/reviewHogSettingsLogic.ts` for the settings loader's retry behavior.
**Found:** The `stamphog` alias already runs on `PRODUCT_DB_FAIL_OPEN_ENGINE` (`data_stores.py:215,220`), a custom Postgres backend whose `ensure_connection` (`failopen/base.py:28-45`) checks a Redis-backed circuit breaker before every connect and raises `CircuitOpenError` in microseconds once the breaker is open — it does not wait for the 3-second `connect_timeout`. The breaker state lives in Redis and is shared by every pod (`db_circuit_breaker.py:147-156`), and it opens after only `PRODUCT_DB_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` (default 3) failures fleet-wide, not per worker. The comment at `data_stores.py:172-175` states this design exists specifically so "one product's outage can't exhaust the shared worker pool" — the exact failure mode this issue describes.
**Found:** `get_stamphog_connected` (`settings.py:71-81`) already wraps the call in `try/except Exception: return False`, and the surrounding comment documents this as a deliberate fail-soft choice, not an oversight.
**Impact:** Only a small, bounded burst of requests (roughly the fleet-wide failure threshold, 3 by default) can pay the full 3-second connect delay while the breaker is still closed; every request after that fails in microseconds for the whole outage. This is a pre-existing, purpose-built platform guarantee that applies to any product-DB caller, not a gap this PR introduces or worsens, so "can delay every settings response" overstates the reachable impact. The Kea loader not auto-retrying after recovery is real but is the same one-time-load-until-refresh pattern already used for every other failed load in this scene (`initialLoadFailed` has no auto-retry either), so it is a minor, pre-existing UX pattern rather than a new correctness defect worth a should_fix.

title: Persist the review handoff before publishing
problem: This function sends one broker message and records no durable pending work. The only caller catches publish errors, so a broker outage can lose the initial review permanently. A later TaskRun save can enqueue again, but no later save is guaranteed.
suggestion: Create a durable handoff record in the same transaction as the TaskRun update. Use the `on_commit` publish as an optimization, and sweep pending records until Celery accepts them. Key the record by `task_run_id` so retries stay idempotent.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `queue_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155`), its only caller `_start_stamphog_review` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:210-234`), the `transaction.on_commit` wiring in `handle_task_run_saved` (`receivers.py:126-139`), and whether any other path re-triggers a missed dispatch (webhook carve-out `_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, later `TaskRun` saves, and any periodic sweep).
**Found:** `queue_inbox_pr_review` (`api.py:149-155`) is a bare `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)` with no durable record of the pending dispatch. Its only caller wraps it in `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)` (`receivers.py:224-234`) with the docstring "the broker being down must never surface into the saver" (`receivers.py:213`) — confirming publish failures are deliberately swallowed. No periodic Celery-beat sweep exists for this task (`grep` across `posthog/settings/`, `posthog/tasks/scheduled.py` finds none for `process_inbox_pr_review`/`queue_inbox_pr_review`). The webhook re-review carve-out is explicitly scoped to LATER deliveries only (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`'s own docstring, `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:160-162`: "the initial review is the receiver leg's job"), so it cannot recover a lost initial dispatch if the self-driving PR never receives a further push. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer`-triggering saves only refire when a later save's `update_fields` includes `output` (`receivers.py:85-89`), which is not guaranteed.
**Impact:** A broker hiccup at the exact moment this `on_commit` fires permanently drops the first hosted Stamphog review for that self-driving PR, with only a log line as evidence — an actually reachable, not speculative, failure mode. This is also inconsistent with this product's own established convention: `tasks.py` retries deliberately at multiple points specifically to avoid "silently drop[ping] a legitimate re-review" (e.g. `tasks.py:873-879`, `tasks.py:1155-1165`), while this one dispatch path breaks that pattern without discussion of the trade-off in the PR.
**Priority:** Left at `should_fix` — the consequence is a missed optional first-pass automated review (a human still triages the PR through Inbox), not data loss, a security gap, or a wrong verdict, and it requires a broker outage to coincide with this exact save.

title: The carve-out accepts any bot identity
problem: The carve-out accepts any user with type Bot or a [bot] suffix. This includes Dependabot, Renovate, and third-party apps. The code comment says this identifies the team's GitHub App machine user, but the check does not verify that identity. A forged or stale task link can grant a third-party bot PR the approval bypass.
suggestion: Compare the author login with the configured PostHog Code GitHub App bot login. Use a case-insensitive exact match and require user.type to equal Bot. Fail closed when the expected identity is unavailable. Apply the same check to initial and webhook reviews.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `_is_bot_authored` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:124-127) and its two call sites: the general webhook pre-filter `_review_skip_reason` (tasks.py:229-231, unchanged by this PR) and the carve-out gate (tasks.py:169-172). Also checked the full body of `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks.py:144-215), `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516), and `find_task_run` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-90).
**Found:** `_is_bot_authored` at line 169 is only a cheap early-out — its own comment says "skip the DB work for every human PR on this path" — not the identity check. After it passes, the carve-out still requires: repo-native head (no fork, tasks.py:176-178), a synced+enabled `StampHogRepoConfig` (tasks.py:180-186), and a strict tasks-facade match via `find_signal_implementation_run`, which resolves `find_task_run` on an exact `output__pr_url` match or an exact `branch` + `repository` match (webhooks.py:41-43, 68-76), then re-checks `team_id`, `task.signal_report_id is not None`, and `not task.internal` (api.py:505-509). Only after all of that does it call the acting-reviewer resolver. `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md` states this design explicitly: "Identification is task linkage, never author-login matching... dependabot/renovate/posthog-bot and non-inbox PostHog Code PRs stay refused everywhere," and the carve-out's own docstring (tasks.py:157) repeats "dependabot/renovate/posthog-bot and non-inbox PostHog Code PRs stay refused."
**Impact:** A Dependabot/Renovate/third-party bot PR passes the cheap `_is_bot_authored` check but has no matching `TaskRun.output.pr_url` or `TaskRun.branch` for that exact repo, so `find_signal_implementation_run` returns `None` and the carve-out resolves empty — no bypass is granted. The suggested fix (match the exact bot login) would replace an already-stronger, deliberately-chosen control (unique-PR/branch linkage plus team scoping) with a weaker one, and directly contradicts the documented decision to identify self-driving PRs by task linkage rather than author login. The "stale task link" scenario also does not hold: GitHub PR numbers are never reused, so a stale `pr_url` match only re-matches the same original PR, and a colliding `branch` name would require an already-trusted repo collaborator to guess an internal run's branch name, which is outside this finding's stated threat model.

title: Use late acknowledgement for the idempotent task
problem: The task uses Celery's default early acknowledgement. If the worker exits after acknowledgement, Celery does not redeliver the task. A crash after the `ReviewRun` commit can leave a `QUEUED` row without a Temporal workflow. Repeated TaskRun saves can repair it, but they are not guaranteed.
suggestion: Set `acks_late=True` and `reject_on_worker_lost=True` on this task. The existing head dedupe and queued-run restart make redelivery safe.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the `@shared_task(...)` decorator on `process_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109`), Celery's global config for `task_acks_late`/`task_reject_on_worker_lost` in `posthog/settings/`, and the task body's idempotency (dedupe-by-head-sha and QUEUED-run restart logic at `tasks.py:1198-1221`).
**Found:** No global `task_acks_late = True` setting exists in `posthog/settings/` — Celery's early-ack default applies, so a message is acknowledged the moment a worker picks it up, before any of the function body runs. The codebase already has an established convention of opting individual idempotent tasks into `acks_late=True, reject_on_worker_lost=True` when a crash mid-execution must not lose the work (`posthog/tasks/tasks.py:348-358`, `posthog/tasks/exporter.py:48`, `posthog/tasks/usage_report.py:113-114`, `posthog/tasks/ai_observability_usage_report.py:683-684`) — `process_inbox_pr_review` does not follow it. The task's own body confirms it is safe to redeliver: the head-sha dedupe query and the explicit "except a still-QUEUED one, whose post-commit workflow start failed ... restart it instead of stranding it (the start is idempotent)" comment (`tasks.py:1198-1221`) already handle a partially-completed prior attempt.
**Impact:** With early ack, a Celery worker killed mid-task (OOM, pod eviction, a routine rolling deploy — all common events, not rare edge cases) after the message is delivered but before `process_inbox_pr_review` finishes silently drops that delivery; nothing redelivers it. The task's own idempotent restart logic exists specifically to make redelivery safe, so the missing `acks_late=True`/`reject_on_worker_lost=True` leaves that safety net unused for a failure mode (worker restarts during deploys) that will occur routinely in this environment.

title: The initial path does not verify that the task produced the PR
problem: The invariant says both trigger paths verify PR linkage before stamping inbox provenance. The receiver treats caller-writable `TaskRun.output.pr_url` as proof that the run produced the PR. `process_inbox_pr_review` does not compare the PR with the task repository, branch, head repository, or expected bot author. A `task:write` caller can target another configured PR. Stamphog can then approve it through the self-driving carve-out.
suggestion: Resolve `task_run_id` through the tasks facade before stamping provenance. Require the same team, signal report, task repository, native head branch, and expected App bot author. Reject all mismatches. Add tests for cross-repository, fork, human-authored, and unrelated-bot PR URLs.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1246), its caller `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155), the review_hog receiver that sources `pr_url` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-141, :210-234), the `TaskRun.output` write path (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py: `set_task_run_output`, `_apply_caller_output`, `_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS`), and the webhook re-review leg's equivalent gate `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-215).
**Found:** `process_inbox_pr_review` only parses the caller-supplied `pr_url`, resolves a `StamphogRepoConfig` by the parsed repository, fetches the PR, checks `state == open`, and stamps `inbox_review` (including the caller-supplied `task_run_id`, `signal_report_id`, `acting_user_id`) with zero independent verification — no bot-author check, no fork/head-repo check, and no lookup of `task_run_id` against the tasks facade (tasks/tasks.py:1130-1234). Contrast this with the webhook re-review leg, `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks/tasks.py:144-215), which performs exactly the checks the issue asks for: `_is_bot_authored`, a fork-safety `head_repo == repo` comparison, and a call to `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516) that independently re-derives the run from GitHub's own webhook-supplied `pr_url`/`head_branch`/`repository`, matching team + signal-report + non-internal task. `pr_url` on `TaskRun.output` is caller-writable via the `task:write`-scoped `set_output`/`update` endpoints (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1092-1121, :1058-1090) — `_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS` only protects `pr_merged` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1770), not `pr_url` — so nothing stops a `task:write` caller (including the sandboxed agent's own scoped credential, which the product's own trust model treats as running over untrusted content) from pointing a legitimate, non-internal, signal-report-linked task's `output.pr_url` at an unrelated PR.
**Impact:** Because the initial receiver leg skips the linkage check the webhook leg already implements, a caller that controls `TaskRun.output.pr_url` for any signal-report task can redirect Stamphog's self-driving carve-out onto an arbitrary PR in a Stamphog-configured repo, bypassing the bot-author refusal, fork-safety check, review-mode gate, and author-write-permission gate that would otherwise apply to that PR (per this same file's carve-out invariant, lines 110-112) — up to and including a real GitHub approval. The PR description itself claims step 4 of Case 1 "checks the PR is really ours (our bot, no fork, the task's repo)", but that check is only implemented on the webhook path, not the receiver path this AGENTS.md section documents as already covered. This is a genuine, reachable auth/tenant-trust gap, not speculation.

title: The documented toggle gate conflicts with the feature contract
problem: The PR contract enables Stamphog when any assigned reviewer opts in. This text requires the selected acting reviewer to opt in. The implementation also checks only that reviewer. A secondary assigned reviewer cannot enable the review.
suggestion: Check all resolved assignees. Prefer the task creator when that person opted in. Otherwise use the first opted-in assignee for attribution. Update both documents and test a primary assignee who is off with a secondary assignee who is on.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the pre-PR and post-PR versions of `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py` (`gh pr diff 75215`), specifically `_resolve_acting_reviewer`/`_resolve_assigned_reviewer` and its call sites for both `review_inbox_prs` and the new `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle, plus the docstring's citation of "maintainer decisions, 2026-07-02/03".
**Found:** the single-canonical-acting-reviewer resolution (`task_created_by_id` if they are among the resolved reviewers, else the first resolved reviewer — receivers.py:206-207) is **pre-existing**, not introduced by this PR. Before this diff it already gated the older `review_inbox_prs` toggle the same way (`if not ReviewUserSettings.load(team_id, acting.id).review_inbox_prs: return None`, per the PR's own removed-lines diff). This PR only reuses that same established resolver for the new `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle (`resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`, receivers.py:144-156), for consistency with the existing mechanism. The README text under review ("gated by the acting reviewer's per-user `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle") accurately describes this actual, deliberate, long-standing behavior.
**Impact:** the issue's premise — that the README/implementation conflict with "the feature contract" — inverts the actual source of truth. The authoritative contract is the codified, dated maintainer decision behind the single-acting-reviewer model (docstring, receivers.py:166-168), not the PR's own informal cover-letter phrasing ("at least one of the assigned users"), which is a loose paraphrase, not a spec. The README documents the real implementation correctly, and the suggested fix would change well-established, intentional pre-existing behavior shared with the unrelated `review_inbox_prs` toggle — out of scope for this PR and contradicted by the code's own historical-decision comment. This is a mistaken premise, not a live doc/implementation defect.

title: A queued initial review can run after opt-out
problem: The invariant says that disabling the toggle stops new runs. `process_inbox_pr_review` trusts the earlier receiver check and does not check the current setting. A delayed or retried job can create a run and post an approval after opt-out.
suggestion: Recheck current assignee settings in `process_inbox_pr_review` after task-link verification and before `ReviewRun` creation. Return when no assigned reviewer remains opted in. Test disabling the setting after dispatch but before worker execution.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1246) end to end, the `StamphogReviewWorkflow.run` activity sequence (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/workflow.py:45-100+), and the timing constants in `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/constants.py`.
**Found:** the toggle (`stamphog_review_inbox_prs`) is checked exactly once, synchronously, inside `handle_task_run_saved` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126) before the Celery dispatch. `process_inbox_pr_review` itself never re-reads `ReviewUserSettings` — it only resolves the repo config, fetches the PR, dedupes on head, creates the `ReviewRun`, and starts the workflow (tasks.py:1136-1234). The workflow's activity list (`dismiss_stale_approvals` → `signal_review_started` → `fetch_review_context` → up to `STAMPHOG_BOT_REVIEW_MAX_POLLS`×`STAMPHOG_BOT_REVIEW_POLL_SECONDS` (10×30s = ~300s) of in-flight-bot polling → `run_review_in_sandbox` (`RUN_REVIEW_TIMEOUT` = 30 min) → `post_verdict`) contains no activity that re-checks the acting reviewer's toggle before posting an approval. Only the separate webhook re-review leg (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, tasks.py:144-215) re-resolves the toggle via `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()`, and only for later pushes — not for the initial queued run.
**Impact:** the Celery task can also be delayed by its own retry/backoff (`max_retries=3`, and `countdown=max(e.retry_after or 0, 60)` on GitHub rate limits — tasks.py:1150,1162,1165,1237), stacking on top of the multi-minute workflow window above. A user can toggle `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` off after the initial trigger fires but before the run reaches `post_verdict`, and the run still completes and can post a real GitHub approval — directly contradicting the invariant text under review ("A toggle switched off mid-PR stops new runs", AGENTS.md:106) for the initial-review path specifically. This is a reproducible, realistically-sized race window (potentially tens of minutes), not a theoretical edge case, and it produces an unwanted, non-consented GitHub approval — a genuine correctness/consent gap worth fixing.
**Priority:** kept at `should_fix` — the window is real and the consequence (an unwanted standing approval) is concrete, but it requires a same-team user to flip the toggle within a multi-minute race rather than being an externally exploitable or cross-tenant security hole, so `must_fix` is not warranted.

title: Initial inbox reviews trust a caller-controlled PR URL
problem: TaskRun.output.pr_url is writable through the task run API. Signal tasks are controllable by every team member. This task trusts that URL and never loads task_run_id. It does not compare the PR with the task repository, work branch, head repository, or expected bot identity. The code then stamps inbox_review, which lets the engine bypass bot and draft gates. A project member without GitHub access can target an unrelated human or fork PR and cause a real approval.
suggestion: Load TaskRun with task_run_id and team_id before any GitHub call. Verify its signal report, task type, and repository. Parse the URL with GitHubIntegrationBase.parse_pull_request_url. Require a repo-native head and the configured PostHog Code bot. Use a server-only PR attestation because the output and branch fields are caller-writable. Store inbox_review only after all checks pass.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the full body of `process_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1245`) for any lookup of `task_run_id`, bot-identity check, or fork-safety check; the TaskRun `output` write path (`products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1069-1121`, `serializers.py:167-180,671-674`); the authorization gate on that path (`products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:22-46`); and where self-driving implementation tasks set `origin_product` (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:250`).
**Found:** `process_inbox_pr_review` takes `task_run_id` as a parameter but never loads the `TaskRun` row with it — it is only copied into the `inbox_review` output dict for provenance (`tasks.py:1176-1181`, `tasks.py:1229`). The function's only real gate is that `pr_url`'s repository has a synced+enabled `StamphogRepoConfig` (`tasks.py:1140-1147`); it never checks the PR author is a bot, never checks `pr.head.repo` against the expected repository (no fork-safety check, unlike the sibling webhook path's explicit one at `tasks.py:176-178`), and never cross-checks the PR against the originating task's `repository`. It then unconditionally stamps `output={"inbox_review": inbox_review}` (`tasks.py:1223-1229`), which is exactly the marker the engine reads to bypass the bot-author and draft gates (per `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md`'s carve-out description) and, separately, to skip the write-permission check outright (`tasks.py:967-969`: `author_below_write = False if inbox_review is not None else ...`). On the write side, `TaskRunUpdateSerializer.output` and `TaskRunSetOutputRequestSerializer.output` are plain unrestricted `JSONField`s (`presentation/serializers.py:179`, `671-674`) reachable via `PATCH .../runs/{id}/` and `PATCH .../runs/{id}/set_output/`, gated only by `task_control_q` (`visibility.py:30-46`): `Q(created_by_id=user_id) | Q(created_by__isnull=True) | Q(origin_product__in=TEAM_VISIBLE_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS)`. `TEAM_VISIBLE_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS` includes `SIGNAL_REPORT` (`visibility.py:22-27`), and self-driving implementation tasks are created with exactly `origin_product=SIGNAL_REPORT` (`auto_start.py:250`) — so, by design, ANY team member (not just the task's creator) can write `output.pr_url` on these tasks, with no format or authenticity validation (`validate_set_output` only checks an optional `json_schema`, which these tasks don't set).
**Impact:** Any team member who can write to a signal-report task's output — which, per the confirmed authorization model, is any member of the team — can set `pr_url` to an arbitrary open PR (a colleague's human PR, or an external contributor's fork PR) in any repo the team has Stamphog enabled for. The next `TaskRun` save routes through `handle_task_run_saved` → `queue_inbox_pr_review` → `process_inbox_pr_review`, which fetches that PR, stamps it with `inbox_review` provenance, and queues a review that bypasses bot-author, draft, and write-permission gates and injects a TRUSTED prompt context — potentially producing a real GitHub approval on a PR the attacker has no legitimate relationship to. This is a concrete, reachable authorization gap, not a theoretical one, and it contradicts the product's own stated invariant that inbox provenance is stamped only by "linkage-verified" trigger paths.

title: Webhook linkage trusts a user-writable PR URL
problem: find_task_run returns an output.pr_url match before it checks the webhook head branch. The task API lets callers write output.pr_url. Therefore, the verified webhook branch does not validate a URL match. A team member can attach an unrelated bot PR to a signals run in the same repository. Its next webhook receives the self-driving carve-out and skips review-mode and author-permission checks.
suggestion: Do not use output.pr_url as proof of provenance. Scope the TaskRun query by team_id from the start. Require the webhook head branch to match a server-attested work branch. Alternatively, add a protected PR-link attestation that only the verified GitHub webhook can write.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `find_signal_implementation_run` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-517`, new in this PR), `find_task_run`'s `pr_url` branch (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-59`), the one caller of `find_signal_implementation_run` — stamphog's webhook re-review carve-out `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-215`) — and the writability of `TaskRun.output.pr_url` via the general task API (`presentation/serializers.py:179,671-674`, gated only by `task_control_q` in `products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:30-46`, which grants control to any team member for `SIGNAL_REPORT`-origin tasks, confirmed at `products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:250`).
**Found:** `find_task_run` (`webhooks.py:41-59`) matches purely on `output__pr_url=pr_url` (plus an optional repository filter), with no distinction between a `pr_url` written by the verified GitHub webhook backstop (which requires HMAC signature verification and a same-repo, non-fork head before writing) and one written through the freely-writable, unauthenticated-in-content `set_output`/`update` task API. `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` passes the webhook's own real `pr.get("html_url")` into this matcher (`tasks.py:191-196`), so a team member who plants that exact URL into their own `SIGNAL_REPORT`-origin task's `output.pr_url` makes `find_task_run` return their task's run whenever GitHub delivers a later event (synchronize/reopen) for that URL — regardless of whether their task ever produced that PR.
**Impact:** This is reachable, though narrower in blast radius than the sibling finding on `process_inbox_pr_review` (which has no bot-author or fork check at all): `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` still requires `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (`tasks.py:169-172`, GitHub-reported, not attacker-controlled) and a non-fork head (`tasks.py:176-178`) before reaching the lookup, so the target must already be a genuinely bot-authored, same-repo PR (e.g. a Dependabot/Renovate PR). Within that constraint, a team member can still make Stamphog treat an unrelated bot's PR as self-driving and skip review-mode and author-write-permission gates on it — a real, concrete authorization gap in newly added code, not a hypothetical one.

title: Truthy JSON can enable the approval carve-out
problem: The code treats every nonempty JSON value as enabled. A value such as `"false"` bypasses the bot-author refusal and the draft gate. This flag can lead to a GitHub approval, so malformed input must fail closed.
suggestion: Accept only the literal JSON boolean `true`, such as with `context.get("self_driving_review") is True`. Treat all other types as `False`. Add regression cases for strings, numbers, arrays, and objects.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every producer of the hosted context JSON's `self_driving_review` key. There is exactly one caller of `build_reviewer_invocation` in the whole codebase: `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451`, passing `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`.
**Checked:** `build_reviewer_invocation` (products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:86-138) stores that already-Python-`bool` value straight into the `context` dict (line 131) and serializes it with `json.dumps(context, ...)` (line 137) — a Python `True`/`False` always serializes to the JSON literal `true`/`false`, never a string, number, array, or object.
**Checked:** `review_local.py::main` reads that same file back with `json.loads(...)` (line 396), and `run()` is only ever invoked with the dict produced by that parse — there is no second entrypoint or test helper in this repo that constructs a `context` with a non-boolean `self_driving_review` and feeds it to `run()`.
**Found:** `inbox_review` itself (the source of the coercion in activities.py:451) is only ever `None` or the non-empty provenance dict built in `_InboxCarveOut.provenance` (tasks.py:140, 208-215) — so `bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` is always a clean `True`/`False`, and that is the value that reaches the JSON.
**Found:** `review_local.py` itself documents this at lines 316-320: the flag "rides in on the hosted context JSON, stamped by the server only for runs positively linked to a ... signals implementation task," i.e., it is server-controlled trusted input, not attacker-controlled PR content. `review_local.py` also runs as the sandbox's first command (see `command` in `build_reviewer_invocation`), before any PR-controlled code executes, so nothing in the sandbox can rewrite the context file ahead of the read either.
**Impact:** the failure mode described (`"false"` or another truthy-but-wrong JSON value reaching `self_driving_review`) cannot occur with the current, sole call path — the value is a genuine Python `bool` from creation to serialization to deserialization. This is a speculative type-confusion scenario that the existing call site and type already rule out, not a reachable bug; `bool(context.get(...))` here is redundant defensive coding on an already-guaranteed type, not a fail-open security hole.

title: Stamphog ignores opted-in secondary reviewers
problem: The new Stamphog gate checks only the single ReviewHog acting reviewer. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` prefers the assigned task creator or the first resolved assignee. If that user opted out, both paths skip the review even when another assigned user opted in. This does not implement the stated rule that any assigned user's opt-in enables Stamphog.
suggestion: Resolve all assigned users and select a Stamphog actor from users with `stamphog_review_inbox_prs=True`. Preserve the current single-actor rule for ReviewHog. Prefer an opted-in task creator, then the first opted-in assignee. Use the same selection for the initial dispatch and webhook resolver. Add a multi-assignee test where the first reviewer is off and the second is on.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (`receivers.py:159-207`), `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (`receivers.py:144-156`), `handle_task_run_saved` (`receivers.py:111-126`), and the full test suite in `products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py`.
**Found:** The single-canonical-reviewer model is a documented, deliberate, and tested maintainer decision, not an oversight. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer`'s docstring (`receivers.py:167-171`) states explicitly: "the first resolved reviewer is canonical (maintainer decisions, 2026-07-02/03)" and that this one user's toggles "gate the respective reviews." `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:228-238`) asserts exactly the scenario this issue calls a bug — canonical reviewer `bob` opted out, secondary reviewer `alice` opted in — and asserts no review starts, with the comment "a later reviewer's opt-in must not hijack whose options the review runs with." This PR extends the identical, pre-existing pattern to the new Stamphog toggle rather than introducing new logic: `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` reuses the same `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` call (`receivers.py:149-151`, "Same acting-reviewer resolution as this module's own trigger"), and `test_resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer_keys_on_the_stamphog_toggle` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:371-387`) and `test_the_two_toggles_gate_their_reviews_independently` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:313-343`) confirm and lock in this same single-actor behavior for Stamphog.
**Impact:** The PR body's casual phrasing ("at least one of the assigned users has it enabled") is imprecise summary copy, not the actual spec — the code, its docstrings, and its passing tests unambiguously implement and codify the single-acting-reviewer rule on purpose, consistently across both toggles. Changing Stamphog to scan all assignees, as the suggestion proposes, would break design consistency with the already-shipped ReviewHog toggle and contradict an explicit, dated maintainer decision plus its regression test. Investigating the actual code shows the premise (this is unintended/broken logic) is mistaken.

title: Internal implementation runs never qualify
problem: Signals auto-start creates production implementation tasks with internal=True. This predicate rejects every such task. Neither initial reviews nor later webhook reviews run for their pull requests.
suggestion: Identify implementation tasks through the recorded implementation association. Allow internal auto-start tasks and non-internal manual tasks. Continue to reject research and repository-selection tasks by association type.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the only implementation-task creator for the signals pipeline, `_create_implementation_task_if_absent` (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:198-265`); the `Task.internal` field's actual semantics (`products/tasks/backend/models.py:207-209`, a visibility flag, never flipped after creation); `find_signal_implementation_run`'s predicate (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:508-509`); the sibling predicate in `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py`; and the base branch's version of that same file for comparison.
**Found:** `_create_implementation_task_if_absent` creates the real implementation task with `internal=True` unconditionally (`auto_start.py:261`, comment: "Internal so the run stays out of the default task list") — there is no other code path that creates a signal-report implementation task, and nothing ever flips `internal` back to `False` afterward. `find_signal_implementation_run`'s `task.signal_report_id is None or task.internal` (`api.py:508-509`) therefore rejects every genuine implementation task, not just the research/repo-selection plumbing tasks it is meant to filter out. The base branch's prior version of `receivers.py` documents this exact fact correctly — "Report research and repo selection share both signal_report_id and internal=True with it [the implementation task], so only ai_stage tells them apart" — and used `(instance.state or {}).get("ai_stage") != "implementation"` as the actual discriminator. This PR's diff (`git diff master HEAD -- products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py`) replaces that correct `ai_stage` check with `if task.internal: return`, on a new comment claiming "the auto-start implementation task is the only non-internal signal-report task" — which `auto_start.py:261` directly contradicts.
**Impact:** With this predicate, neither review_hog's own plain inbox trigger (`receivers.py`) nor the new stamphog carve-out (`find_signal_implementation_run`) can ever match a genuine self-driving implementation run, since its task is always `internal=True`. No self-driving PR would ever receive an initial or re-review under either mechanism — a complete, confirmed regression of the feature this PR adds, not a speculative edge case. The existing test fixture in `products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py` (`internal: bool = False` default, `internal_pipeline_task` negative case at line 273) encodes the same wrong assumption, so it does not catch this against real production task-creation behavior.

title: The queue callback imports the full Stamphog worker stack
problem: This callback runs on the TaskRun save path. `queue_inbox_pr_review` imports `products.stamphog.backend.tasks.tasks` before it publishes the Celery message. That module loads the GitHub and Temporal clients at module scope. A clean post-setup import took about 0.6 seconds locally. Each web process pays this delay once and retains those modules.
suggestion: Publish the task by its registered name with `current_app.send_task`, as other cross-product facades do. Alternatively, add a lightweight task wrapper that imports the handler only inside the Celery worker. Keep the live save path limited to message serialization and publication.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155` (`queue_inbox_pr_review`), `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1-32` (module-scope imports), `products/stamphog/backend/logic/github_client.py` and `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/client.py` (what those imports pull in), and `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/__init__.py` (Celery autodiscovery wiring). Also checked for an established lighter-weight alternative pattern in the codebase.
**Found:** `tasks.py` imports `StamphogGitHubClient` (`logic/github_client.py`, pulling in `jwt`, `requests`, and `posthog.egress.github.transport`) and `execute_stamphog_review_workflow` (`temporal/client.py`, pulling in `temporalio.common` and `asgiref.sync`) at module scope (`tasks.py:28,30`). `queue_inbox_pr_review`'s own existing comment (`facade/api.py:144-146`) already acknowledges this exact weight: "the Celery task module drags the GitHub client and temporal client onto the import path, which must stay off this facade's light import surface" — confirming the reviewer correctly traced the dependency chain, not a mistaken premise.
**Found:** The current deferred import inside `queue_inbox_pr_review` only prevents the *worse* case — eager loading at `django.setup()` for every process, since `has_reviewable_repo_config` lives in the same `facade/api.py` module and is imported at module scope by `review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:16`. It does not remove the residual, one-time cost paid by whichever process's `transaction.on_commit` callback first calls `_start_stamphog_review` → `queue_inbox_pr_review`, since `transaction.on_commit` runs synchronously in the calling process/thread.
**Found:** A lighter, established alternative already exists in this codebase for exactly this cross-product dispatch problem: `products/customer_analytics/backend/facade/api.py:1120-1129` dispatches via `current_app.send_task("customer_analytics.process_custom_property_sync", kwargs=...)`, and its `COMPROMISES.md` documents the identical rationale — "By-name dispatch also keeps the product ... out of the ... worker's process, since core imports nothing from here." A second precedent exists at `posthog/temporal/data_modeling/activities/succeed_materialization.py:122`.
**Impact:** The save-path callback for a hot model (`TaskRun`) pays a real, avoidable one-time import cost (github/jwt/requests/temporalio) purely to publish a Celery message, when a proven `send_task`-by-name pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase would avoid importing `tasks.py` (and its heavy dependencies) from the caller entirely. This is a genuine, actionable reliability/performance cleanup consistent with an existing team convention, not speculation or overengineering — `should_fix` is the right severity given it is a one-time per-process cost rather than a per-request one.

title: A broker failure permanently drops the initial review
problem: After Celery producer retries end, `_start_stamphog_review` only logs a publication error. The TaskRun save still returns success, so the caller does not retry. No pending record remains for a sweeper. A PR with no later output save can miss its initial review permanently.
suggestion: Persist a pending dispatch keyed by team and task run before returning. Let a worker retry pending rows with backoff. Mark each row sent only after the broker accepts it. A scheduled reconciliation for PR targets without a Stamphog run is another option.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `_start_stamphog_review` (`receivers.py:210-234`), `queue_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155`) for where the `ReviewRun`/`PullRequest` rows actually get created, the sibling `_start_review` path (`receivers.py:237-273`) for comparison, and both `review_hog`'s manual trigger endpoint (`api/reviews.py:623-668`) and stamphog's own API surface for any user-facing recovery path.
**Found:** `queue_inbox_pr_review`'s own docstring (`facade/api.py:136-142`) confirms the `PullRequest`/`ReviewRun` rows are created only *inside* the Celery task (`process_inbox_pr_review`), so nothing is persisted before the broker publish. `_start_stamphog_review` (`receivers.py:224-234`) wraps `.delay()` in a bare `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)`, with no DB row, no retry, and no reconciliation hook for a failed publish.
**Found:** Unlike ReviewHog's own leg, Stamphog's inbox integration has no manual recovery path: `review_hog`'s `trigger` action (`api/reviews.py:623-668`) only starts a ReviewHog review, never a Stamphog one, and `products/stamphog/backend/api/` does not exist — there is no endpoint a user could call to manually re-request a Stamphog review for a specific PR. The only two paths that can ever start one are this receiver's initial dispatch and stamphog's own webhook re-check on a later `synchronize`/`reopened` push (per the module docstring, `receivers.py:20-23`).
**Impact:** A self-driving PR that never receives a follow-up push (common for a small, immediately-mergeable change) permanently loses its Stamphog review the moment a transient Celery broker outage outlasts the producer's own retry window — with no operator-visible pending state and no user-facing way to recover it. Celery broker blips of this duration are a realistic, not speculative, failure mode, so this meets the bar for a genuine reliability defect (swallowed error hiding a real failure, missing handling for a failure mode that will occur) rather than defensive paranoia. `should_fix` is the right severity: the gap is silent and permanent but scoped to an optional, currently-experimental safety check rather than data loss or a broken core flow, and ReviewHog's independent leg can still provide review coverage on the same PR when its own toggle is on.

title: Repeated output saves create duplicate GitHub fetches
problem: The receiver publishes a Stamphog task whenever an output save still contains `pr_url`. The TaskRun output API preserves that URL. Later agent turns therefore enter this path even when the URL did not change. `process_inbox_pr_review` must fetch the PR from GitHub before it can deduplicate by head SHA. A burst creates redundant Celery jobs and GitHub requests.
suggestion: Coalesce dispatches by `(team_id, task_run_id)` before publication. Use a short debounce with a pending generation, so the worker processes the latest state once. Schedule another run when the generation changes to preserve the lost-webhook backstop.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `handle_task_run_saved`'s early-exit guard (`receivers.py:85-89`, `126-139`), and `process_inbox_pr_review`'s full implementation and docstring (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1175`), including its Celery task decorator.
**Found:** `process_inbox_pr_review`'s own docstring (`tasks.py:1125-1128`) confirms the exact mechanism the issue describes: "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL, so dedupe keys on the PR's CURRENT head" — and the code fetches the PR from GitHub (`tasks.py:1158-1159`, `StamphogGitHubClient(...).get_pr(...)`) *before* it can compute that head SHA and dedupe (`tasks.py:1170-1174`), exactly as the issue states. This re-fire behavior is a deliberate lost-webhook backstop (documented, not accidental), but the team's own comment only justifies *why* refires happen, not that each refire's GitHub fetch is free.
**Found:** `@shared_task(ignore_result=True, max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)` (`tasks.py:1109`) carries no unique-task-id, throttle, or debounce option — every `.delay()` call from `queue_inbox_pr_review` is an independent enqueue with its own independent GitHub fetch; nothing coalesces same-`(team_id, task_run_id)` dispatches before publication.
**Impact:** A burst of `TaskRun.output` saves carrying the same unchanged `pr_url` (plausible whenever a save touches `output` for unrelated reasons, since the early-exit only checks whether `output` was touched, not whether `pr_url` changed) produces one redundant Celery job and one redundant GitHub API call per save, consuming the installation's shared GitHub rate-limit budget and worker capacity for no behavioral gain. This is a real, concretely-traceable inefficiency rather than speculation, so it clears the bar for a kept finding — the reviewer's own `consider` priority is well-calibrated: the waste is bounded per burst, doesn't corrupt state (the later dedupe still no-ops extra runs), and the underlying repeat-refire pattern is an intentional, already-accepted backstop design, so this is a genuine but low-urgency efficiency cleanup, not something to raise higher.

title: Apply TaskRun scope before selecting a row
problem: `find_task_run` executes `.first()` before this function applies the team and self-driving filters. If an ineligible matching row sorts first, this function returns `None` and ignores an eligible row. Unrelated TaskRuns can therefore stop a self-driving re-review. The branch fallback also searches the global TaskRun table without an indexed team prefix.
suggestion: Apply `team_id`, signal report, and `internal` filters before `.first()`. Pass `team_id` into `find_task_run` or implement a scoped facade query. Pin this decision read to the writer. Add a scoped branch index if this path keeps the branch fallback.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `find_task_run` (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-90`) and its caller `find_signal_implementation_run` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-517`); the `TaskRun` model's indexes (`products/tasks/backend/models.py:1147-1174`); and whether multiple `TaskRun` rows can genuinely share one `output.pr_url`.
**Found:** `find_task_run`'s `pr_url` branch (`webhooks.py:41-57`) filters only on `output__pr_url=pr_url` plus an optional `repository` match, orders by `terminal_rank, -created_at`, and calls `.first()` — with no `team_id`, `signal_report_id`, or `internal` filter applied inside the query. `find_signal_implementation_run` (`api.py:504-509`) applies those checks only AFTER the single row is already selected (`run.team_id != team_id`, then `task.signal_report_id is None or task.internal`), so if a row that fails those checks outranks the actually-eligible row in `terminal_rank, -created_at` order, the function returns `None` even though an eligible row exists elsewhere in the result set. Multiple rows sharing one `pr_url` is not purely theoretical here: the function's own comment (`webhooks.py:36-39`) documents this exact shape already happening for wizard resumes ("a terminal original and its live resume can both claim the same PR URL"), and the previously-confirmed writability of `output.pr_url` for any `SIGNAL_REPORT`-origin task (via the task API) gives a second, concrete way for a second row with the same `pr_url` to appear. The branch-only fallback (`webhooks.py:64-76`) also has no index on the plain `branch` column and no `team_id` filter — only `state__wizard_head_branch` and `output__pr_url` have dedicated partial indexes (`models.py:1153-1164`).
**Impact:** This is a genuine query-construction defect distinct from (though compounding with) the writable-`pr_url` authorization gap: even setting aside malicious writes, a coincidental or resumed duplicate row can silently make a legitimate self-driving PR's re-review resolve to `None`, blocking a review that should have run — a real wrong-result scenario, not speculative. `should_fix` is proportionate since the observable effect here is a missed/blocked re-review (availability), milder than the unauthorized-approval consequence already covered by the separate `must_fix` findings on the same lines.

title: Resolve equal GitHub timestamps before superseding
problem: The stale check rejects only a strictly older `updated_at`. GitHub timestamps have second precision, so an old fetch and a new push can share the same value. In that race, the old task passes this check, supersedes the new-head run, and starts an old-head run. The final head guard prevents a stale approval, but the current head can finish without a review.
suggestion: Add a second ordering signal for equal timestamps before `_supersede_prior_runs`. One option is to record the fetch completion time and reject a different-head run created after it. Another option is to re-fetch when the timestamps match but the latest run has a different head.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `process_inbox_pr_review`'s staleness recheck and supersede call (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1186-1222`), `_upsert_pull_request`'s conditional refresh UPDATE (`tasks.py:319-363`), and the equivalent, pre-existing pattern in the webhook leg `process_pull_request_event` (`tasks.py:1010-1054`) for comparison.
**Found:** `_upsert_pull_request`'s WHERE clause (`tasks.py:352`) uses `payload_updated_at__lte=incoming_updated_at` (`<=`, not `<`), so two payloads with an identical `updated_at` can both satisfy it in sequence — each caller's local `pr_obj.payload_updated_at` ends up equal to its own `incoming_updated_at`, not strictly less. `process_inbox_pr_review`'s recheck (`tasks.py:1190-1197`) only bails when `pr_obj.payload_updated_at > incoming_updated_at` (strict), so an equal-timestamp case falls through to `_supersede_prior_runs(pr_obj)` (`tasks.py:1222`) regardless of which of the two competing snapshots is genuinely current. The webhook leg has the identical structural gap — its own comment states the design assumption explicitly: "Equal timestamps proceed (a redelivery of the current head)" (`tasks.py:1014`) — so this is a pattern the new receiver leg mirrors rather than something isolated to it, but the new leg is more exposed to it: it does its own live `get_pr()` fetch (`tasks.py:1159`) that can be overtaken mid-flight by a genuinely newer, concurrently-processed webhook push with a coincidentally equal (second-resolution) timestamp — a plausible race specifically for self-driving agent PRs, which push commits in rapid succession.
**Impact:** The reviewer's own analysis is confirmed: `post_verdict`'s current-head-vs-GitHub check (the stale-approval invariant) stops a wrong approval from landing on the stale head, so this is not a security bypass. But the up-to-date review it wrongly superseded is gone, and the stale run's own verdict gets refused at post time, so the PR's actual current head ends up with no review at all until a further push retriggers one — a real, if narrow-window, availability gap matching "missing handling for a failure mode that will occur," not a hypothetical.

title: ReviewHog startup runs before the Stamphog-first dispatch
problem: Django runs these callbacks immediately in autocommit and serially inside a transaction. The code connects to Temporal before it publishes the Stamphog job. A slow Temporal service delays Stamphog. An import failure prevents its callback from running. This reverses the stated Stamphog-first flow.
suggestion: Publish the Stamphog job first. If Stamphog must gate ReviewHog, start ReviewHog from the Stamphog result. Otherwise use robust callbacks and catch deferred import failures.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `handle_task_run_saved` (`receivers.py:114-139`), `_start_review` (`receivers.py:237-273`) and `_start_stamphog_review` (`receivers.py:210-234`) for their unguarded deferred-import statements, Django's `transaction.on_commit`/`run_and_clear_commit_hooks` semantics, the PR body's "Problem" section for the claimed "Stamphog-first" contract, and `test_the_two_toggles_gate_their_reviews_independently` for the actual documented design intent.
**Found:** The "reverses the stated Stamphog-first flow" framing does not hold up: no code, docstring, or test states a required dispatch order between the two `on_commit` callbacks. The PR body's "first stage" language (`## Problem`) describes Stamphog as a conceptually cheaper/faster review *stage* in a staged product rollout, not a runtime ordering contract on these two fire-and-forget triggers. `test_the_two_toggles_gate_their_reviews_independently` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:313-343`) explicitly asserts the opposite of the suggestion's first remedy: "the two toggles ... gate their reviews independently: neither may imply, block, or replace the other." Gating ReviewHog on Stamphog's result, as the suggestion proposes, would directly contradict this deliberate, tested design.
**Found:** The "slow Temporal service delays Stamphog" claim is technically true (both dispatches run via sequentially-registered `on_commit` callbacks, so a blocking Temporal connect call in `_start_review` delays when `_start_stamphog_review` fires) but immaterial: both dispatches are fire-and-forget triggers (a workflow-start call and a Celery `.delay()`), while the actual review work (sandbox + LLM) each triggers takes minutes — a few seconds of relative dispatch-order skew has no bearing on which review's *verdict* lands on the PR first.
**Found:** The one concretely valid point is narrower than stated: `_start_review`'s deferred imports (`receivers.py:254-255`) and `_start_stamphog_review`'s deferred import (`receivers.py:222`) both sit **outside** their own `try/except Exception` blocks. Per Django's `run_and_clear_commit_hooks`, a non-`robust` `on_commit` callback that raises stops the remaining queued callbacks in that transaction from running — so if `_start_review`'s import (registered first, when `review_inbox_prs` is on) ever raised, it actually would swallow the newly-added `_start_stamphog_review` callback entirely. This coupling is only consequential now that a second `on_commit` callback exists in this receiver, so it is a genuine (if narrow) regression risk introduced by this PR.
**Priority:** Downgraded to `consider`: the dominant claim (ordering violates a stated contract, and its proposed fix of reordering/gating) is not well-founded and its primary remedy would regress a deliberate, tested design. The one valid mechanism (unguarded import in an earlier `on_commit` callback can silently drop a later one) is real but depends on a stable, already-in-production import spontaneously failing at runtime — a low-probability trigger, not a `should_fix`-level risk. `robust=True` (or moving the imports inside the try/except) is a low-cost, worthwhile hardening still worth keeping on record.

title: Re-check the opt-in inside the delayed task
problem: The receiver checks `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` before it publishes the Celery job. This task never checks the setting again. A broker delay or retry can let the user disable the setting before this code runs. The task still creates or restarts a run that can post a real GitHub approval. ReviewHog rechecks its matching setting when its workflow resolves, so the two paths have different opt-out behavior.
suggestion: Reload the task run through the tasks facade. Use the registered resolver to check the current assignment and setting before the GitHub fetch and dedupe. Return when the resolver returns `None`. Stamp the newly resolved user ID in `inbox_review`. Add a test that disables the setting after queueing and confirms that no workflow starts.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `process_inbox_pr_review`'s full body (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1245`) for any re-check of `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`; the resolver registry (`get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver`, `tasks.py:25`); and whether the sibling ReviewHog inbox path re-checks its own analogous toggle at execution time.
**Found:** `process_inbox_pr_review` takes `acting_user_id` as a parameter (already resolved and toggle-checked by the caller before `.delay()`) and never re-verifies it — it goes straight from the GitHub fetch (`tasks.py:1159`) to dedupe and `ReviewRun` creation (`tasks.py:1198-1230`) using that stale `acting_user_id`, with no call to `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()` anywhere in the function. By contrast, ReviewHog's own plain inbox trigger explicitly re-checks its matching `review_inbox_prs` toggle inside the Temporal workflow at resolve time (`products/review_hog/backend/temporal/workflow.py:434`), with the comment "Trigger-aware opt-outs, read off the resolve-time settings snapshot (mid-run edits can't flip gates)... Inbox re-checks the receiver-side gate here for snapshot-at-resolve consistency" (`workflow.py:424-427`) — confirming the team already treats this exact TOCTOU as worth closing for the twin toggle, but the new `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` path omits the equivalent guard.
**Impact:** The task's own retry/backoff behavior widens this window in practice — `GitHubRateLimitError` retries with `countdown=max(e.retry_after or 0, 60)` (`tasks.py:1160-1162`) and `max_retries=3` general retries — so a reviewer who disables the toggle during a broker delay or a rate-limited retry still gets a real GitHub review/approval posted afterward, contradicting the PR's own stated goal ("turning this off never leaves an approval on code nobody checked"). The consequence is narrower than an unauthorized-access bug (the opt-out came from a cooperating, already-assigned reviewer, not an attacker), which supports keeping this at `should_fix` rather than `must_fix`.

title: Bind the carve-out to the fetched PR
problem: The engine does not bind this flag to the fetched PR's required shape. The hosted path can stamp it for a human-authored or fork PR. Such a PR bypasses the draft gate. The trusted prompt also falsely identifies its source and author.
suggestion: Validate the PR before constructing `Pipeline`. Apply the flag only when the PR is bot-authored and its head repository equals `context["repo"]`. Otherwise, use `self_driving=False` or refuse the review. Add regression cases for flagged human drafts and fork PRs.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the sole producer of `self_driving_review` in the hosted context JSON — `activities.py:451` sets it from `bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, and `build_reviewer_invocation` (logic/reviewer.py:119-138) serializes that server-side value into the sandbox context file. The flag is never derived from PR-controlled content, and the context file is written before any untrusted PR code runs in the sandbox.
**Checked:** the webhook re-review path, which is the actual behavior this chunk adds. `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks.py:144-215) already binds the carve-out to the PR shape BEFORE stamping provenance: `_is_bot_authored(pr)` at tasks.py:169, and the fork-safety check `head_repo.strip().lower() != repo.strip().lower()` at tasks.py:176-178. A human-authored or fork PR resolves to empty provenance, so `inbox_review` is never stamped and the flag stays false.
**Checked:** the receiver leg `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1109-1237). It stamps `inbox_review` for a `pr_url` taken from a non-internal signal-report task's own `output.pr_url` (review_hog receivers.py:93-138) — server-internal state written when the bot's agent opens the PR, not attacker-controlled PR content. Reaching it with a human/fork PR would require compromising the task pipeline, a different trust boundary than the PR content this feature treats as untrusted.
**Found:** the engine's `PRData` (github.py:17-37) carries no head-repository field — only `repo` (the base repo, from `context["repo"]`) and `author_is_bot`. The specific fork check the suggestion asks for ("head repository equals `context['repo']`") is not even implementable in the engine without extending the context, confirming the engine is not the layer designed to make this decision.
**Found:** the design is documented as intentional in `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md` ("The self-driving inbox carve-out"): validation lives in the two linkage-verified server trigger paths, the flag "defaults closed and the Action never sets it," and the hosted server "sets the flag exclusively from the run's persisted inbox provenance ... which only the two linkage-verified trigger paths stamp." Trust-at-the-trigger, consume-downstream is the deliberate architecture.
**Impact:** the premise — "the hosted path can stamp it for a human-authored or fork PR" — is not reachable through the PR-content boundary: the webhook path validates bot + fork, and the receiver path's input is the bot's own server-written task output. The proposed engine re-check is defense-in-depth against a scenario the current call sites already rule out, and the fork half of it cannot be expressed with the data the engine holds. This is speculative / defensive paranoia rather than a concrete reachable defect, so it does not meet the bar.
